title: Office 16 Trusted Location configured in a high-risk directory
description: Detects Office 16 per-user or user-policy Trusted Location paths directed to a drive root, selected download/temporary directories, profile variables or a UNC share.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may configure a broad or writable Office Trusted Location to reduce document security checks for attacker-controlled files.
hypothesis.rationale: Configuration alone does not establish effective trust or execution. Network locations can remain disabled by policy; other Office versions and custom paths are outside scope.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Detects Office 16 per-user or user-policy Trusted Location paths directed to a drive root, selected download/temporary directories, profile variables or a UNC share.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint registry events

triage.summary: Configuration alone does not establish effective trust or execution. Network locations can remain disabled by policy; other Office versions and custom paths are outside scope.
steps: Review the full trusted path, Office application, user, initiating process and whether subfolders are trusted.
Inspect effective Trust Center and Group Policy settings; determine whether any active content was opened from the directory.
Validate the business owner and replace unjustifiably broad trust with a controlled approved location.
false_positives: Approved managed templates, training environments or user workflows intentionally trusting a selected directory.

validation.expected_outcome: Match the bounded event, key/action/path or successful operation combination; reject one-field mutations, lookalikes and absent required fields. Synthetic tests do not establish live telemetry or production performance.

limitations: Configuration alone does not establish effective trust or execution. Network locations can remain disabled by policy; other Office versions and custom paths are outside scope.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
